name: Bea Rial
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: Bea has cleaned most city landmarks without ever being invited to an opening. She likes the ward because somebody always notices when the sea suddenly becomes clearer. Saturday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Bea asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: You can see an old handprint when the sun catches that pane. My daughter left it on a visit years ago. I cleaned the rest and asked the patient whether she minded the hand.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. Bea has one cheek that creases before the other, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Bea draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first during a conversation.
personality: Bea listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To leave or remove the little handprint according to the patient's wishes.
family: Denise Ho is Bea’s half-sibling. Bea makes the call. Denise is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The late crossing*, Denise says, “I lost my license and kept quiet. I contribute by watching the driver's children for the round trip.”
connections: Mika Drew. The last obstacles between the bed and the view are a sticky rail and a pane with an old handprint.

reactions.situation: A different patient needs the same porter
reactions.response: Bea checks which part can wait and makes sure the other patient hears about the delay.
reactions.asWritten: A different patient needs the same porter. Bea checks which part can wait and makes sure the other patient hears about the delay.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Bea offers to walk to the next staffed place together, at the stranger's pace, to ask about another ride.
